  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently
in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be
allowed only to observe and address the City Council Meeting of (October 26, 2021, at 2:00
P.M. Or 1:00 P.M. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic means, as
follows:

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  October 26, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
October 26, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales,
  and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on the
Closed Session Items.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

  *****************
Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/ Joint Powers Authority Secretary
announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint
Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.
   October 26, 2021

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on
  the Agendas, other than the public hearing.

  Ray Howler, commented on a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised to call back
  towards the end of the meeting to address his concern.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at 2:07 p.m.

  PRESENTATION – SENATOR STEVEN BRADFORD (DISTRICT 35). Steven
  Bradford, California State Senator (District 35) provided a Legislative Update on the
  California Senate. Senator Bradford reported $8.5 million dollars, which he secured along
  with the help of Congresswoman Autumn Burke for the Market Street Improvements.
  Additionally, he summarized the Senate Bills that he introduced, including SB 789 and
  seven other bills that the Governor approved, including SB 2, SB 796, SB 567, SB 655,
  SB 694, and SB 26.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at 2:10 p.m.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  October 22, 2021, in the amount of $3,826,560.56 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – REDRAWING OF CITY COUNCIL DISTRICT
  BOUNDARIES, IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE FAIR MAPS ACT. The City
  Clerk announced the next schedule matter was a public hearing to receive public input
  regarding the redrawing of City Council district boundaries, in accordance with the Fair
  Maps Act, and that notices were given in the time, form and manner as required by law,
  an affidavit was on file, and no communications were received.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated October 26, 2021.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk, gave a brief oral report.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:21 p.m.

  Hearing no public comment, Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour
  of 2:21 p.m.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on September 28, 2021,
  October 5, 2021, October 12, 2021, October 12, 2021 (Special), and October 19, 2021, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   October 26, 2021

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1) Big Daddy Enterprises dba Big Daddy’s Kickin Chicken for alleged personal injury;
  (loss of revenue); permitted street closure on May 5, 2021.
  2) Deanna Reed for alleged personal injury; failure to secure mobility device on March
  4, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1, and A-2. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-021 APPROVED – DUDEK.
  Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented recommending approval of
  Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-021 with Dudek, extending the term of the
  agreement to December 31, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-021
  with Dudek. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED – DOOLEY ENTERPRISES, INC. Staff
  report dated October 26, 2021, was presented recommending authorization to issue a
  blanket purchase order to Dooley Enterprises, Inc., for the purchase of practice and duty
  ammunition.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby authorize issuance in a total amount not to exceed
  $200,932 (includes a ten percent (10%) contingency in the amount of $18,267). The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 22-020 APPROVED – GENUINE PARTS COMPANY DBA
  NAPA AUTO PARTS. Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of a four (4)-year cooperative purchase agreement (with the
  option to extend an additional (1) year) with Genuine Parts Company dba NAPA Auto
  Parts for the annual purchase of aftermarket vehicle parts.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 22-020 in an annual amount
  not to exceed $250,000 (total of $1,000,000). The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-205 APPROVED – RIDECO,
  INC. Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented recommending approval of
  Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-205 with RideCo, Inc., extending the term by
  one (1) year (with the option to extend for three (3) additional one (1)-year terms), to
  assist with the operation of a pilot shuttle service.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-205
  in an additional amount not to exceed $1,227,072 (includes a five (5%) contingency in
  the amount of $58,432). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
   October 26, 2021

183  AGREEMENT NO. 22-021 APPROVED – MPD REALTY, INC.; MAYOR
  AUTHORIZED TO SIGN SAID AGREEMENT. Staff report dated October 26,
  2021, was presented recommending approval of the Encroachment Maintenance and
  Removal Agreement with MPD REALTY, INC., to install an American with Disabilities
  Act (ADA) compliant ramp in the public right-of-way in front of the property located at
  417 Centinela Avenue, Inglewood, California.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Encroachment Maintenance and Removal
  Agreement No. 22-021; and 2) Authorize the Mayor to sign said agreement. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-022 APPROVED –
  OPTIMA RPM, INC.  Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented
  recommending award of a contract and approval of an agreement with Optima RPM, Inc.
  (Contractor), for the Police Locker Room Project, per Bid No. CB-21-14.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 22-022 in a
  total amount not to exceed $2,202,310.93 (includes a contingency in the amount of
  $300,000). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  BID NO. CB 20-01 REJECTED – I-405 GATEWAY LANDSCAPE PROJECT;
  REBIDDING OF THE PROJECT AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated October 26,
  2021, was presented recommending rejection of all bids received on January 22, 2020,
  for the I-405 Gateway Landscape Project, per Bid No. CB-20-01.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject bids; and 2) Authorize the rebidding of the
  project. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  RESOLUTION NO. 22-06 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE 2021-2022 FISCAL
  YEAR BUDGETED POSITIONS. Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution amending the 2021-2022 Fiscal Year budgeted
  positions to add an Administrative Analyst to the Police Department Administrative
  Bureau.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that Resolution
  No. 22-06 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2021-22 FISCAL YEAR
  BUDGETED POSITIONS

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACTS AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 22-023 APPROVED –
  KIMLEY-HORN AND ASSOCIATES, INC., AND WILLDAN ENGINEERING.
  Staff report dated October 26, 2021, was presented recommending award of contracts and
  approval of three (3)-year professional services agreements (with the option to extend for
  up to an additional six (6) years, in three (3)-year increments), for the As-Needed
  Professional Engineering Services Project, per Proposal No. RFP 0168.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contracts and approve Agreement No. 22-023, in an

  4
   October 26, 2021

  annual pooled amount not to exceed $4.5 million (total of $13.5 million), with the
  following consultants: a) Kimley-Horn and Associates, Inc.; and b) Willdan Engineering.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 22-024 APPROVED – CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND THE
  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY  METROPOLITAN  TRANSPORTATION
  AUTHORITY (LACMTA); RESOLUTION NO. 22-07 ADOPTED – MAYOR
  AUTHORIZED TO EXECUTE THE MEASURE R FUNDING AGREEMENT,
  AND COMMITTING THE CITY TO COMPLY THEREWITH. Staff report dated
  October 26, 2021, was presented recommending approval of Measure R Funding
  Agreement No. 9200000000MRINGITC between the City of Inglewood and the Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) to accept a
  reimbursement grant, in the amount of $233,700,000, from LACMTA for the Inglewood

  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager, Artie Fields, congratulated the Social
  Media Department led by Thomas Bunn on receiving the Savvy Award for the Best
  Public Service Announcement (PSA), and the Silver Circle Award for being creative with
  the least dollar amount spent for the mask-on COVID 19 video. He also stated that after
  his encouragement to enter, the PSA went viral, capturing the attention of several Raiders
  football players. Mr. Fields read the letters received from two of the players and invited
  Thomas Bunn to speak about his achievements.

  Thomas Bunn, Social Media Administrator, thanked Artie Fields, City Manager, for
  motivating the team to enter the contest. He stated it was a great honor to be recognized
  amongst some of the nation's best communicators and selected for the Savvy Award and
  Silver Circle Award. He also thanked his team, a group of guys composed of filmmakers,
  documentarians, and photographers who love what they do. Brian Walker and Crystal
  McGlover from the Office of Emergency Services, were also thanked for their assistance
  with the connection between local business owners and residents. He further shared the
  inspiration to create the video to remind people to wear their masks to slow the spread of
  COVID-19. Lastly, he thanked the Council for the foresight to document all the events
  that occurred during the renaissance of Inglewood.
